svg.text: 195 Hz - 1.03 kHz (VR1 sets the High / Mid crossover point)
73 Hz - 186 Hz (C3, C4 = 2 x 33nF) (VR2 sets the Mid / Low crossover point)
U3D is the spare section: input grounded, output tied back.
Q1-Q3 shunt each buffer input through R31-R33. A JFET conducts at Vgs=0, so the board powers up MUTED and R40/C16 release it after
SUPPLY BYPASSING - one 100nF ceramic per rail, at each IC
3-Way State Variable Electronic Crossover - ESP P148, retuned, three quad op-amps, SMD build for JLCPCB assembly
After Rod Elliott, Elliott Sound Products, Project 148 (https://sound-au.com/project148.htm). Redrawn for EasyEDA.
All op-amps MC33079 - 3 x SOIC-14 packages. Q = 0.5 Linkwitz-Riley with R3 / R13 = 11k; use 11k2 for exact Q = 0.5, or 5k04 for Butterworth (Q = 0.707).

VR1 and VR2 are dual-gang 20k linear pots wired as rheostats. TP1 / TP2 null at the crossover frequency and may be omitted. VR3/VR4/VR5 are single-gang 10k audio-taper pots wired as attenuators - per-output volume, not part of the filter.

U3A/U3B/U3C buffer each volume pot's wiper, so the output impedance is the op-amp's rather than up to 2.5k of pot track, and the amplifier's input impedance no longer loads the pot or bends its taper. U3D is the unused section, terminated. R28-R30 hold each output at 0 V when nothing is plugged in.

Input impedance is R1 = 47k, a line-level figure: a master volume pot ahead of the board (one dual-gang for a stereo pair, feeding both channels' J2) works properly into it. It is off-board because this board is one channel.
